body:
Makes viola Linux-only. It first sets and pushes the tag multi-os-final on the last three-OS commit, then removes every cfg(windows) and target_os = "macos" arm with its tests and fixtures, the four Windows-only files, vendor/conpty and the Windows target dependencies with their deny entries.
It drops the Windows and macOS CI jobs (test, lint, perf, release, nightly) and the whole windows-mutants workflow. A cfg(unix) arm whose only sibling is gone becomes unconditional, and the census of OS-gated tests is re-pointed or retired.
It makes the two e2e-home free-space floor cases decide on a figure the test controls, not the host's free space, so msrv goes green. No Linux behaviour, exit code, closed word or wire contract moves.
Re-reads at take-up: no multi-os-* tag stands, the four files total 1 146 lines, and every named path stands at HEAD. P3 re-measures the count of OS gates. The masters' OS-target change, a11y-plan included where it names a Windows terminal behaviour, is listed as expected amendments that the wrap writes.

body: The CI integration for CLI output discipline and the TUI boundary: these cases run inside the test job's single instrumented coverage suite, and its gate --require coverage,doctest never allows skips. Once the Windows and macOS test jobs are gone, the ubuntu-latest leg is the only verdict, and the cases must still run there in full.

The tui boundary on the portable-pty outer-PTY driver (path P4, the wheel): viola emits zero bytes of its own, human keystrokes are never blocked past the current atomic paste, and focus, mouse and resize sequences and terminal replies do not take the wheel. Its Linux cases stay as they are. The Windows arms leave: the win32-input-mode mouse report that takes the wheel (F-W3) and the windows-2025 platform fact.

The boundary after a contained vt100 feed panic: no viola literal reaches the outer terminal, and the child's own bytes pass on Unix. The Windows byte reading owed to the retired entry Windows-only live measurements loses its code.

Path P6, the CLI board: the TTY-only behaviours are asserted under the outer PTY on all three OS legs, and the dim-only-on-stale-rows witness runs on ubuntu-latest and macos-latest. After the macOS arms leave, both rest on the ubuntu leg alone.

The error-recovery verification: trycmd pins the unable reason detail plus a final hint: layout for each refusal, and assert_cmd checks the typed exit codes and a hint-free --json. The per-OS carve-outs move: the server-verify peer pid witness (windows-2025 and ubuntu-latest), macOS's euid-mismatch-only word with no peer pid (SERVER_PID_REPORTED), and the socket-directory refusal on ubuntu-latest and macos-latest.

The viola revive --json refusal set shared with run, batch-script-child among them (the .cmd / .bat refusal). If the removal leaves its text naming Windows code that no longer exists, P4 decides whether it changes. Its Linux exit-1 document stays as it is.

The pinned fixed CLI strings (trycmd or literal): a copy change fails CI until the pin is updated on purpose. Any help string, doc comment or refusal text that drops a Windows or macOS word must update its pin knowingly. No Linux closed word changes.

The visual SGR rules (visual-sgr, visual-sgr-stale-row): no SGR of viola's own under non-TTY, NO_COLOR, TERM=dumb, --json, viola run or a passed viola revive, and every span sits beside its word. A cfg(unix) arm over TTY or terminal detection that becomes unconditional must keep this behaviour on Linux unchanged.

The CI platform matrix of section 9 ([windows-2025, macos-latest, ubuntu-latest]) and the per-pipeline-stage row run on all three OS legs. After this chunk ci.yml carries ubuntu-latest alone, and this is one of the expected a11y-plan amendments.

The SLO invariant that the CLI output-discipline invariants (P4, P6) pass on all three OS legs, with the epoch-boundary mutation audit (run --mutants) covering the ones in crate tests. Removing windows-mutants.yml must not drop that audit's coverage on Linux. The three-leg wording is an expected amendment.

The runner named for a11y CI: scripts/agent-run.sh run (or .ps1), and the CI anti-pattern that allows no driver outside scripts/agent-run.* run. If the PowerShell twin leaves, the sh harness stays the only runner.

The a11y-plan text that names a Windows or macOS terminal behaviour, an expected amendment under the masters' OS-target change: the Windows byte reading and F-W3 in the scope summary, the keyboard anti-pattern and the focus order; the testing tool reach rows (NVDA with Windows Terminal or conhost, VoiceOver with Terminal.app); and the per-surface screen-reader table (cli on Windows, macOS and Linux; tui on Windows). Orca with GNOME Terminal stays the Linux target. Each amendment carries the ruling in its sidecar entry.

The tests' zero-flakiness rule (retries 0, #[ignore] banned, no retry-once), through the e2e-home free-space floor cases: they pass or fail by the host's disk, so the fix must make them deterministic on a figure the test controls, never ignore or retry them.

When this chunk removes `nightly.yml`'s Windows and macOS jobs, no a11y case is lost, because the a11y leg lives in `ci.yml` alone. This is the sentence that names the `[windows-2025, macos-latest, ubuntu-latest]` matrix, which the wrap amends.

**2026-09-24-quality-gates** (CLI output-discipline evidence under the CI `coverage` suite) — established that the CLI output-discipline cases run "on all three OS legs" and report in CI inside the per-OS `test` job's single `coverage` suite, gated by `gate --require coverage,doctest`. §1, §9 and §10 carry this wording. Removing the matrix collapses it to the ubuntu-latest leg, which must still run every case. The three-leg wording becomes an expected amendment.

**2026-09-25-pty-wrapper-on-windows** (Windows zero-viola-bytes oracle is literal absence) — split the zero-viola-bytes clause into two oracles: byte for byte against an unwrapped run on Linux and macOS, and viola's literals absent on windows-2025, because ConPTY emits its own preamble. §6 now reads "zero SGR of viola's own". This chunk removes the Windows arm only. The byte-for-byte Unix oracle stays as the sole assertion, and §3 and §6 are where the ConPTY text gets amended. §1 was kept verbatim, which is a precedent.

**2026-09-28-mutation-testing-to-the-epoch-boundary** — §10 says the epoch-boundary mutation audit (`run --mutants`) covers the P4 and P6 invariants that live in crate tests. When `windows-mutants.yml` leaves, that audit must still cover them on Linux. The §10 invariant's "all three OS legs" is an expected amendment.

**2026-09-29-sideloaded-conpty** — the Windows zero-viola-literals check names both ConPTY hosts: the sideloaded `OpenConsole.exe` preamble, and the inbox fallback that `conpty_sideload`'s tampered case drives. `tests/conpty_sideload.rs`, `crates/viola-pty/src/sideload.rs` and `vendor/conpty/` all leave in this chunk. The text in §3 Keyboard test harness and §6 CLI equivalent that credits these hosts' bytes now names code that no longer exists, so it is an expected amendment.

**2026-10-04-the-wheel** — defined case (3) as step-wise, with the wheel probed by `answer` (exit 13 means driver, 10 means human). Linux and macOS got the full assertion. `windows-2025` got the F-W3 platform fact: focus reports are swallowed, and the injected mouse report takes the wheel. It also added the Keyboard ban's ConPTY key-down clause. This chunk removes only the F-W3 arm and that ban clause. The step-wise Linux probe and the closed non-editing list stand unchanged.

**2026-10-07-t05-47-07-wrap** — re-pointed the real Windows terminal's mouse-report measurement to the route entry "Windows-only live measurements" (blocked on an interactive Windows host). That entry is now retired, and its master hits are re-pointed under the scope's CARRY. This §3 keyboard-harness sentence is one of those hits.

**2026-10-07-send-waits-out-the-paste-hint** — added the outer-PTY case `send_under_the_paste_hint_a_human_key_during_the_gate_wait_wins` under boundary clause (2). It is sequenced on records, never on a timer. The extract's acceptance requires it to run and pass on ubuntu-latest inside `coverage`, never skipped or ignored, after any OS arm around it leaves.

**2026-10-08-first-live-test-and-self-drive** — §1's NVDA line calls Windows "the first target" (it used to say "live-supported target"). It also recorded a supplemental live Linux reading of the takeover clause. Under the Linux-only OS target, the NVDA wording in §1 and §7 is an expected amendment. Orca with GNOME Terminal stays the Linux target.

**2026-10-09-t14-44-30-wrap** — cites "Windows-only live measurements" by route title instead of a bare route number. This is a precedent for how master text cites route entries. The title citation is exactly what the wrap's `rec.py find --text 'Windows-only live measurements'` sweep finds and re-points.

On Unix the start writes the settings override and passes `--settings`. On Windows it writes none. The Windows clause leaves with its code, and the Unix reading stays unchanged.

Each leg's `gate --require coverage,doctest` is its own verdict, and the failure conditions include `suite-skipped` and `suite-missing`. The zero-flakiness rule bans `#[ignore]`. §11 bans a `suite` value or a second a11y driver outside `scripts/agent-run.* run`. Trimming the matrix keeps ubuntu-latest as the only verdict. No a11y case may become a skip. If `agent-run.ps1` leaves, `.sh` must remain the only runner.

This chunk removes the windows-2025 arm, and the Unix-only no-ESC assertion falls under the scope's "made unconditional" rule.

**2026-10-26-server-verification-before-any-frame** (the six frame verbs' server-verify refusal; the plugin against an impostor wrapper) — introduced the exit-21 server-verify refusal and the hook/MCP impostor entity. Its gate falls under the made-unconditional rule, and it must keep running in full on ubuntu-latest.

**2026-10-26-home-and-code-bearing-file-integrity** (strict-modes refusals as scope entities, their text, witnesses and pinned pairs) — the six frame verbs, `run` / the revive start and `verify` refuse a home or instance that fails strict modes. body_fields.quote: **[PTY] portable-pty `=0.8.1` pinned behind viola's own `pty` seam (spawn · read · write · resize · wait · kill).** Child exit is detected on the process handle, never on EOF, because ConPTY does not close the output stream on exit. If 0.8.1's Windows `kill()` misbehaves, the fallback is `TerminateProcess` on `child.process_id()` via windows-sys.

Child exit is detected on the process handle, never on EOF; on Windows x64 the ConPTY is sideloaded, failing open to the inbox one, and every `viola` process restricts its DLL search to System32; viola never holds, queues or re-orders a human key behind a resize and never answers DA1 itself. `viola_pty::pty_backend()` reports `conpty-sideload` after a successful pre-load, else `conpty` (Windows) or `openpty`. body_fields.why: the Windows persist retry decision and the ConPTY companions' shared replace and held-open retries leave with the Windows arms, and replace_private on Linux must keep its behaviour (no retry, a failure leaving the target as it was).
body_fields.quote: On Windows a `persist` refused with raw OS error 5 (a reader holding the target open, as measured at chunk 2026-09-27-hooks-to-normalised-events research.md M1 under every share mode) is retried every 10 ms, re-persisting the same temp file, at most `viola_state::fs::REPLACE_ATTEMPTS` = 100 attempts (an attempt count, never a time bound); any other error returns at once. The loop sits in the private `replace_private_retrying`, which takes the decision to retry a failed rename (from its raw OS error) from its caller; `replace_private_with` passes `retry_replace(_, HOST_IS_WINDOWS)`, so the product's behaviour is the one above and the loop's attempt bound is exercised by a unit case on every host (chunk 2026-10-13-epoch-4-survivors). `replace_private_shared` is the variant for files every concurrent start of one version writes identically (the plugin files, the Windows x64 ConPTY companions under `bin/<version>-<hash>/conpty/`): a replace that fails counts as done when the target already holds exactly those bytes. The pinned copy's absent-copy write is never a replace: it is the no-clobber `place_private_new` (below). The companions' held open (`FILE_SHARE_READ` only) retries a Win32 error 32 (sharing violation) under the same `REPLACE_ATTEMPTS` bound (`retry_open`, `open_held_waiting`), as measured at chunk 2026-09-29-sideloaded-conpty: two concurrent first starts, the refusal lasting 5-11 ms after the other start's write, 0 of 6 pairs over companions already written.

body_fields.why: the Windows SQOS Identification open and the named-pipe half of the IPC decision leave, the Unix-socket half staying as it is on Linux.
body_fields.quote: On Windows the client connects only through the SQOS Identification open (windows-sys `CreateFileW` with `SECURITY_SQOS_PRESENT | SECURITY_IDENTIFICATION | FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED`, adopted by `Stream::try_from`), never interprocess's default connect, so a squatted or rogue server cannot impersonate the client; a non-overlapped handle adopted this way hangs (as measured at chunk 2026-09-25-security-prerequisites). Rationale: one API over named pipes and Unix sockets, sync and Tokio flavours, and no daemon. macOS caps socket paths at about 104 bytes.
on Windows the client connects only through the SQOS Identification open, never interprocess's default connect.

body_fields.why: the Linux SO_PEERCRED pid and start-time server check before the first frame must stay while the Windows pid arm and the macOS SERVER_PID_REPORTED carve-out lose their code.
body_fields.quote: `viola_channel::Client::server_pid` and `tokio_client::TokioClient::server_pid` return the connected stream's peer pid through interprocess's `peer_creds().pid()`: Linux `SO_PEERCRED`, Windows `GetNamedPipeServerProcessId` on the client end the SQOS Identification open adopts, none on macOS, where `SERVER_PID_REPORTED` is false; they write and log nothing. Every frame-writing client compares that pid and the process's OS start time with the snapshot's before its first frame (§Standard Contracts, Channel methods), so on Linux and Windows a squatted or rogue server is never sent a frame either.

body_fields.why: the macOS no-peer-pid Matches verdict is the macOS carve-out whose code leaves, Linux's server_verdict comparison unchanged.
body_fields.quote: On macOS no peer pid is reported, so `viola_state::liveness::server_verdict` returns `Matches` with no comparison: the recorded gap, named and owned by no route entry. The macOS client euid and socket-directory checks, and the 0755-directory exit-cause case, stand built, so on macOS `server-verify-failed` means an euid mismatch alone.

body_fields.why: PEER_EUID_REPORTED's cfg!(unix) gate is made unconditional, a peer whose euid cannot be read staying refused, and the Windows DACL control leaves.
body_fields.quote: `viola_channel` exports `peer_euid_admitted`, `peer_admitted` and `PEER_EUID_REPORTED`, the last `cfg!(unix)`: `peer_euid_admitted(observed, own, reported)` is `!reported || observed == Some(own)`, so a peer whose euid cannot be read is refused where it is reported, and on Windows the DACL and the pid comparison stay the controls. `Client::server_euid` and `TokioClient::server_euid` supply the observed euid, writing and logging nothing.

body_fields.why: as the Unix gates become unconditional, the accept loop's peer-euid decision must stay injected with no env, flag or feature seam, a refused stream dropped before any frame.
body_fields.quote: The wrapper's `accept_loop` filters `incoming()` by `admitted(peer_euid_of(stream))`, so a refused stream is dropped on the accept thread, before its worker thread and any frame, reading end-of-file, writing no line, nothing on the terminal and moving no wheel; `Server::serve` injects the decision, `peer_admitted`, as a `type Admission` through the private `serve_admitting`, with no env, flag or feature seam.

body_fields.why: check_socket_dir's off-Unix Ok(()) arm leaves and its Unix half loses its gate with its Linux verdicts unchanged.
body_fields.quote: `viola_state::strict::check_socket_dir` takes one `symlink_metadata`: an absent path passes, an unstattable one is `Refused::Unreadable`, then `socket_dir_verdict` reads a symlink as `Refused::Symlink`, a non-directory as the fixed-message `Refused::NotADirectory` and anything else by the read rule; it never chmods, a refused directory stays as found, and off Unix it returns `Ok(())`. `check_endpoint_dir` is that check on a recorded endpoint's parent.

body_fields.why: the hook's connect runs the checks whose Unix gates become unconditional, and each refusal must still exit 0 with no body, the hook contract the chunk re-asserts.
body_fields.quote: The event and dialog paths, once their instance check has passed ([Hook Contract]), share one connect: `replay::read_snapshot_or_replay` (a replayed or absent snapshot is an endpoint not reached: the hook fails open with `channel-unreachable`), then `check_endpoint_dir` on the recorded endpoint, then `Client::connect_by`, then `peer_admitted(client.server_euid())`, then `verify_server` (§Standard Contracts, Session liveness). A refused directory gets no frame: the hook records `socket-dir-refused` and exits 0 with no body. A serving process of another euid, or whose pid or OS start time is not the snapshot's, or a check that cannot be made, gets no frame: the hook records `server-verify-failed` and exits 0 with no body, the event lost as for an unreachable endpoint.

body_fields.why: hook's contract (exit 0, no body, no stderr) must come out of the removal unchanged on Linux, and the dialog hold's Windows leg owned by the retired entry is an expected amendment.
body_fields.quote: **[Hook Contract] Hooks fail open.** Exit 0 with a JSON body is a decision. Exit 0 with no body is no decision (the `unverified-cli` degrade: the dialog renders for the human). Exit 2 is never produced. `hook` exits 0 at once when `VIOLA_NAME` is absent.
Any failure prints and writes nothing; stderr is always empty and the exit always 0

A sync dialog hook waits at most the dialog hold (`dialog_hold_s`, 60–3600 s, default 60; ceiling PROVISIONAL, owner: "Version done-check"; its Windows leg, owner: "Windows-only live measurements"), the dialog then rendering for the human.

body_fields.why: a dialog hook whose server check fails must still send no hook.dialog and exit 0 with no body on Linux once the macOS server-check carve-out leaves.
body_fields.quote: A dialog hook whose server check fails (the serving process is not the recorded wrapper, or the check cannot be made) sends no `hook.dialog` and exits 0 at once with no body, so the dialog renders for the human (its log lines: §Occupied Resources, `diagnostics/`).

body_fields.why: The embedded ConPTY companions, src/conpty.rs, vendor/conpty and pin_companions are the Windows-only code and files the chunk removes, the pinned exe's rules staying.
body_fields.quote: On Windows x64 the binary also embeds Microsoft's ConPTY companions (`src/conpty.rs`: `include_bytes!` of `vendor/conpty/<version>/x64/{OpenConsole.exe,conpty.dll}`; the package version, the nupkg SHA-256 and the two file SHA-256s have that file's text as their one home) and writes them write-if-absent to `bin/<version>-<hash>/conpty/` (`viola_state::pin::pin_companions`; never overwritten). At every start each companion is opened with `FILE_SHARE_READ` only and re-hashed in full against its pin, and the handles are held until the spawn. Unlike the exe, a mismatched companion never refuses the start: it is left as found, never loaded, and the child runs on the inbox ConPTY ([PTY]).

Child exit is detected on the process handle, never on EOF; on Windows x64 the ConPTY is sideloaded, failing open to the inbox one, and every `viola` process restricts its DLL search to System32; viola never holds, queues or re-orders a human key behind a resize and never answers DA1 itself. body:
Makes viola Linux-only: sets and pushes the tag multi-os-final on the last three-OS commit before any removal, after re-reading that no multi-os-* tag stands locally or on origin.
Removes every cfg(windows) and target_os = "macos" arm with its tests and fixtures, the four Windows-only files (1 146 lines, re-read), vendor/conpty/, the Windows target dependencies of the root and crate manifests with their deny.toml entries; a cfg(unix) arm whose only sibling left loses its gate.
Removes the Windows and macOS CI jobs of ci.yml and nightly.yml, the whole windows-mutants workflow and any pre-push or harness step run only for those OSes; re-points or retires the OS-gated test census.
Makes the two e2e-home backing harness cases decide on a free-space figure the test controls, never the host's, so msrv goes green; re-measures the cfg-gate pattern count and closes the msrv failure against run ci#41930831242.
Changes no Linux behaviour (exit codes, closed words, wire contracts, hook contract); the plan names the masters' OS-target amendments as expected amendments the wrap writes.

scripts/orphans-check.sh and its probes (a file gated on a target no CI triple compiles, the cfg(windows)/cfg(unix) file-pair control): with CI on Linux alone, any Windows-gated file left behind trips it, and its control must still fire.

body:
Makes viola Linux-only. First it sets the tag multi-os-final on the last commit that still holds the three-OS code and pushes it to origin, before any removal commit. It re-reads at take-up that no multi-os-* tag stands and that the four Windows-only files hold 1 146 lines.
Removes every cfg(windows) and target_os = "macos" arm with its tests and fixtures, the four Windows-only files, vendor/conpty/, and the cfg(windows) target dependencies with their deny.toml entries. Any cfg(unix) arm whose only sibling is gone loses its gate.
Removes the Windows and macOS jobs from ci.yml and nightly.yml, deletes windows-mutants.yml whole, and removes any pre-push or harness step that runs only for those OSes. Re-points or retires the census of OS-gated tests.
Makes the two viola-e2e harness cases that read the host's real free space against the e2e-home floor decide on a figure the test controls, so the msrv job goes green. P3 closes this against ci#41930831242 on abf00915.
Changes no Linux behaviour, closed word, exit code or wire contract. The masters' OS-target change, including the obs-plan's per-OS logging rows, is the wrap's amendment, and this chunk's plan names it as expected.

body: The CI platform and matrix: the windows-2025 / macos-latest / ubuntu-latest matrix shrinks to ubuntu-latest. Each remaining Linux job keeps its gate steps G1 to G4, each its own bash run step copied verbatim into ci.yml.

The CI step order and conditions on the remaining Linux test and perf jobs. Tests come first, then G2 and G4 under if: always() with homes kept. Then come the harness capture on failure(), the secret-scan step under if: always(), and the diag-<os>, harness-<os> and junit-<os> uploads gated on secret-scan success, with the secret-scan-<os> hit report uploaded on scan failure.
The nightly.yml jobs that stay: the weekly cargo deny advisories job and the fuzz job (120 s per target, fuzz/artifacts/ uploaded on failure() only). Only the Windows and macOS jobs leave.
The dispatch-only windows-mutants.yml, which is the boundary audit's Windows mutation leg. It is deleted, and the mutation gate (run --mutants, survived mutants in obs code) stays on Linux.

The perf budgets on the per-OS perf job, which now has a Linux leg only. run --perf still times the five hook rows, gate --require perf requires all five, and the hyperfine max stays under the 1.0 s budgets with VIOLA_NAME set and a home under target/e2e-home/.
The error budget and its measurement: zero panic lines by G2, zero G4 schema-conformance failures and zero secret-scan hits, read from the in-job gate exit codes on the Linux jobs that remain.

Gates that the removal edits must still pass. cargo deny (Tokio, C-crate, veil toggle and banned obs crates) runs after the Windows dependencies and their deny.toml entries leave. G3 (no panic = abort in Cargo.toml, cargo config or workflows) runs over the edited manifests and workflows. Clippy disallowed-macros, print_stdout, print_stderr and dbg_macro also apply, as does scripts/lint-probes.sh.

The multi-platform-exporter-compat trigger (the same file sink and line schema on every OS) and the obs-plan's per-OS rows. Examples are the ConPTY / openpty and named pipe / Unix socket OS APIs, the windows-sys TerminateProcess fallback on the viola-pty entity, and the 0600 / 0700 rule with its Windows home-DACL arm. These are the expected amendments the wrap writes, and the chunk's plan names them.

The run start scenario's ConPTY sideload companions: the sideload_fallback field on process-start (strict-modes-failed on a refused conpty/ companion) and the closed words conpty-sideload and conpty. They name code this chunk removes. P3 lists each one, and P4 decides it against the masters' change.

The wait / last and MCP server-verification paths. The macOS carve-out (an euid mismatch alone, no peer pid) leaves with the macOS arm. On Linux, the peer-pid and euid comparison, server-verify-failed, socket-dir-refused and strict-modes-failed details, exit 21 and instance-unreachable stay unchanged. No env, flag or feature seam may force a refusing peer-euid decision.

Linux wire and log contracts stay fixed. The closed event enum, the detail code catalog, schemas/diag-line.v1.json and schemas/diag-detail.v1.json keep every Linux value, and the typed exit set 0, 1, 2, 10–14, 20 and 21 stays. Any OS words in the schemas are left for P3 to list.

The PTY seam on Linux: process-start for the claude child, process-exit from the handle-wait thread and never on reader EOF, and exit_source kill-fallback. These are unchanged once the Windows TerminateProcess fallback leaves viola-pty.

The run start refusal pair written through src/human.rs refuse. The .cmd / .bat refusal is Windows text and stays only where it still names live code. P3 lists it, and the fixed two-line stderr pair keeps its shape for the refusals that remain.

The hook contract, which the removal must not move: exit 0, no body, no stderr, and the silent no-op without VIOLA_NAME. The NEVER-log floor and the zero-unlogged-panics invariant also stand as they are.

The e2e-home rule that every integration-test viola home lives under target/e2e-home/, so G2, G4, the secret scan and the diag upload cover it. The harness free-space fix must keep the homes there and keep the 0600 / 0700 owner-only checks those two cases assert.
The msrv job and the MSRV floor of 1.96 (D-22). The job must go green on Linux once the two harness cases stop depending on the runner's real free disk.

The agent-readable consumption path through the harness logs and status commands, which name scripts/agent-run.sh with a .ps1 twin. Whether the PowerShell twin leaves with the Windows CI steps is P3's to read and P4's to decide. The sh harness path stays.

The fake agent as the only CI agent: viola verify runs in CI only against the fake agent, and G2's one exemption is the fake-agent seam's forced panic at src/cmd/hook/seam.rs. Live sessions are 0 for this chunk.

body_fields.convention: each CI gate is its own run step with shell bash, copied verbatim into ci.yml. G2, G4 and the secret scan run if: always(), and a failed test step never skips them.
an artifact upload runs only after the secret-scan step passes, uses an action pinned by commit SHA and checked by zizmor, and keeps retention-days 7. A failed scan uploads the hit report instead.
every new or changed integration test keeps its viola home under target/e2e-home/, so the gates and the secret scan cover it.
tests and telemetry assertions run with retries = 0 and no retry-once policy. Every verdict is an exit-code-setting assertion, never human review.

body: **2026-09-24-supply-chain-and-workflow-gates** — §9 Platform: `ci.yml` stays the single push/PR workflow, and the scheduled `nightly.yml` sits beside it. This chunk cuts Windows and macOS jobs from both workflows, so §9's Platform line is the text the wrap's per-OS amendment re-words. `nightly.yml` stays, with Linux jobs only.

**2026-09-24-quality-gates** — §9 Platform: `nightly.yml` runs advisories plus the fuzz time-box. §8 item 6 admits the nightly `fuzz/artifacts/` upload on failure, from the synthetic corpus only. This chunk edits `nightly.yml` and keeps its `fuzz` job, so that upload must stay `failure()`-only and corpus-synthetic after the OS legs leave.

**2026-09-24-observability-gates** — Retired the inner-allow exemption. Raw `event!` is now caught by a fail-closed grep in `scripts/lint-probes.sh`, proven both ways, which runs on the Linux lint leg, and a `lint-probes.sh` failure is a build failure (§10). That Linux lint leg is what remains after the Windows and macOS lint jobs are cut, so it must keep running the probes.

**2026-09-24-workspace-tree-and-code-graph-planes** — Admitted the `ci.yml` `supply-chain` artifact (`deny.json`, `deny-fuzz.json`, `zizmor.json`) as an unscanned upload, by content: cargo-deny and zizmor diagnostics only, no absolute path. This chunk edits `deny.toml` and the manifests, and the `cargo deny` output it changes is this artifact. The guard clause stays binding.

**2026-09-24-diagnostics-plane** — Schema default-deny is a top-level `unevaluatedProperties: false` in `schemas/diag-line.v1.json`, and `diag-detail.v1.json` is self-contained. body_fields.why: The chunk makes the Unix-only settings override and the statusline shell-out unconditional, and they must keep exactly this shape and stay the only shell-out.
body_fields.quote: `instances/<ViolaName>/settings.json` is the per-session statusline override. It holds `{"statusLine":{"type":"command","command":"<pinned path> hook statusline"}}`, never the user's command.
`snapshot.json` stores `statusline_command`, the user-written shell string that `hook statusline` reads through `VIOLA_DIR` and runs through a shell. This is the only shell-out in viola.

body_fields.why: The Windows pipe arms and the macOS carve-out leave, and every Linux frame-writing client must still run the strict-modes check, the socket-directory check, the peer euid decision and the pid and start-time comparison before its first frame.
body_fields.quote: As built, on Linux and Windows every frame-writing client (CLI `send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause`, `release`, `link`, `unlink`; `viola hook`'s event and dialog paths; `viola mcp`'s `send` / `wait` / `last` / `answer` tools) compares the connected peer's pid and that process's start time with the snapshot's `pid` and `started_at` before its first frame, and sends no frame on a mismatch or a check it cannot make. Each first runs the instance's strict-modes check (`check_instance`: the CLI verbs through `client::refuse_untrusted`, `viola hook` before its obs init, the `viola mcp` tools before `live_endpoint`), a refusal sending no frame, and then reads the snapshot through `read_snapshot_or_replay`, a replayed or absent snapshot giving no endpoint and so no frame; ahead of that comparison, on Linux and macOS, each runs the socket-directory check on the recorded endpoint before connecting (a refusal `socket-dir-refused`, no frame) and the peer euid decision past the connect (a refusal `server-verify-failed`, no frame); macOS, where the peer reports no pid, compares no pid or start time, the named carve-out, owned by no route entry.

On Unix the socket sits in the per-user 0700 directory, not in world-writable `/tmp`; a directory another user owns, a loosened one or a symlink is refused by the socket-directory check, with no bind on `run` and no frame on a client.
`server-verify-failed` (Linux, Windows and macOS, on macOS an euid mismatch alone); `socket-dir-refused` (the socket directory of the recorded endpoint refused).
Per-instance named pipes (Windows) or Unix domain sockets (a verified per-user 0700 directory, never the `/tmp` or `$TMPDIR` root); no Linux abstract namespace.
v1 intends to trust every process of the same OS user and no other; there is no per-connection authentication, the self-reported `from` authenticates nothing, and the endpoint name is predictable.

body_fields.why: The chunk must remove the cfg(windows) listener DACL arm with its windows-sys use, while this text stays in the plan as the unsupported OS's and no Linux listener property changes.
body_fields.quote: The listener gets an explicit protected DACL, `D:P(A;;GA;;;<user-SID>)(A;;GA;;;SY)`: the user SID + SYSTEM only.

IPC access control (Windows) — the listener gets an explicit protected DACL granting the user SID and SYSTEM only; the logon SID is deliberately not added, since the boundary v1 promises is the OS user; remote clients stay rejected, the first-pipe-instance behaviour is kept and the handle is not inheritable.

body_fields.why: The Unix IPC arm must stay whole and act on Linux exactly as before when its cfg(unix) gate goes, keeping the 0700 per-user directory checked before bind and connect, the chmod 0600 after bind, its closed refusals and its fail-open hook, with only the macOS wording losing its code.
body_fields.quote: **Primary control:** the socket lives in a per-user directory with mode 0700: `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/viola/` on Linux, `$TMPDIR/viola/` on macOS, and `/tmp/viola-<uid>/` only as a fallback. The endpoint becomes `<dir>/viola-<h12>.sock`. **Directory check:** before bind, and again before any client connect, `lstat` the directory and require owner == `geteuid()`, `mode & 0o077 == 0` and not a symlink. On failure `run` refuses to start (exit 1), CLI/MCP clients report `instance-unreachable` with `detail` `socket-dir-refused` (the CLI exit 21), and `hook` fails open (exit 0, empty streams, one `hook-decision` of `detail` `socket-dir-refused` at WARN) without writing any frame. **Socket-directory failure at bind:** a failed create and a refused check read one code: `run` and the start of `revive` exit 1 with `socket-dir-refused` and one `process-exit` of that `detail`; a `Server::bind` failure is outside this code. **Secondary control:** the socket file is chmod 0600 right after the bind, on every Unix OS. `ListenerOptionsExt::mode(0o600)` is not used: interprocess 2.4.4 returns `Unsupported` on macOS, which fails the bind, and ignoring it would leave the macOS socket at the umask mode. `try_overwrite` stays off. Linux abstract namespace is never used.

IPC access control (Unix) — the socket lives in a per-user 0700 directory, checked before bind and before any client connect (owner, mode, not a symlink), and is chmod 0600 right after the bind; a failed check refuses `run`, reports `instance-unreachable` to clients and fails `hook` open; `try_overwrite` stays off and the Linux abstract namespace is never used.
`check_endpoint_dir` is the check on a recorded endpoint's parent, the one helper the bind and the three client seams share.

`socket_dir_ready` runs `check_endpoint_dir`, creates the parent only when absent, then checks again, so a race's loser reads the same. It runs before any snapshot, child or `Server::bind`, and the start of `revive` shares it; its refusal is the **Socket-directory failure at bind:** clause of IPC access control (Unix).
**Auth approach:** OS-user ambient trust, enforced per OS, on the IPC endpoints and `~/.viola/`.

body_fields.why: The off-Unix `Ok(())` arm of check_socket_dir must leave with the other OSes' arms, and the verdict made unconditional must keep exactly its absent, unreadable, symlink, non-directory and read-rule outcomes.
body_fields.quote: `viola_state::strict::check_socket_dir` makes one `symlink_metadata` read of the path: an absent path passes and an unstattable one is `Refused::Unreadable`; then the plain `socket_dir_verdict` reads a symlink as `Refused::Symlink`, a non-directory as `Refused::NotADirectory` ("a trusted state path is not a directory"), and anything else through `unix_read_verdict`. Off Unix `check_socket_dir` returns `Ok(())`.
The socket-directory check never chmods: a refused directory stays as found.

body_fields.why: The server-side peer euid drop is a Unix arm the task keeps whole, so it must still drop a foreign-euid peer on the accept thread before any frame once its gate goes.
body_fields.quote: On every accept, `stream.peer_creds()`; if `euid() != geteuid()`, drop the connection before reading a frame.

The drop filters `incoming()` in `accept_loop` by the peer's euid decision on the accept thread, before the stream's worker thread and before any frame: the peer reads end-of-file, and no line and nothing on the terminal is written.
IPC server-side peer check (Unix) — on every accept, a peer whose euid differs from the server's is dropped before a frame is read.

body_fields.why: The Linux client must keep the euid check, the SO_PEERCRED peer pid and the start-time match against the snapshot on every seam, before the first frame of any method, with its closed refusals unchanged.
body_fields.quote: **Unix identity check:** `peer_creds().euid()` must equal `geteuid()` (checked at `cmd::client::connect`, the `connect` of `cmd::hook` and the `frame` of `viola-mcp`, through `peer_admitted`; a peer whose euid cannot be read is refused, and a refused euid reads `server-verify-failed`), and where available (Linux/FreeBSD) `peer_creds().pid()` must equal the snapshot `pid`, with the sysinfo start-time match (built on Linux, the `SO_PEERCRED` peer pid).

**Timing:** all of this runs before the first frame of any method is written on the connection, including `hook.event` notifications (UserPromptSubmit, Stop and PostToolUse carry prompt text, `last_assistant_message` and tool data) and `wait`/`last` requests, not only `send`, `answer` and `hook.dialog`.

**On mismatch** (or a check that cannot be made): no frame is written; the CLI frame verbs exit 21 `instance-unreachable` (the CLI refusal, below) and write one `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:21, detail:"server-verify-failed", during:"connect"}` WARN line; MCP returns `instance-unreachable` with `detail` `server-verify-failed` and writes no line; `hook` fails open (exit 0, no body, its `hook-decision` line carrying `server-verify-failed`). No line or output holds a pid, start time, path or endpoint.
On every client seam the order is the directory check, the connect, the peer euid decision, then the server verification against the snapshot.

body_fields.why: The macOS carve-out and its code must leave with the macOS arms, and no remaining Linux client path may inherit its skipped pid and start-time comparison.
body_fields.quote: **macOS:** `peer_creds()` gives no pid, so verification there is euid + the verified 0700 socket directory, with no pid check. This is accepted for v1 (macOS is CI-only, brief O5) and recorded as a known gap for the public version.

on Linux and macOS the client also checks the recorded endpoint's socket directory before the connect, a refusal reading `socket-dir-refused`, and past the connect admits only a peer of its own euid, an unreadable peer refused, a refusal reading `server-verify-failed`, each sending no frame; macOS compares no peer pid or start time, the named carve-out, owned by no route entry, so there `server-verify-failed` means an euid mismatch alone.

body_fields.why: The Windows SQOS client open and the named-pipe server-pid identity check must leave with their cfg(windows) arms, leaving no default-connect path behind on Linux.
body_fields.quote: **Windows client open:** open the pipe through windows-sys ` CreateFileW(..., SECURITY_SQOS_PRESENT | SECURITY_IDENTIFICATION | FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED, ...) `, then adopt the handle with `interprocess::os::windows::named_pipe::local_socket::Stream::try_from(OwnedHandle)`.
**Windows identity check:** the connected stream's peer pid (the observed server pid, below) must equal the snapshot `pid`, and sysinfo's process start time must equal snapshot `started_at`.

body_fields.why: The Unix strict-modes arm, if made unconditional, must keep refusing exactly the same writable, foreign-owned and readable paths, in every process, before the first read under the home.
body_fields.quote: refuse when the home, `instances/<name>/`, `bin/`, `plugin/` or `ledger/`, the `bin/<version>-<hash>/` and `plugin/<version>-<hash>/` folders the process uses or writes (including the plugin folder's `hooks/` and `.claude-plugin/` subfolders, which hold `hooks.json` and `plugin.json`), or a trusted file itself (`snapshot.json`, `ledger/stamps.json`, the pinned `viola`) is group- or world-writable or not owned by euid (ssh StrictModes style).

**Read rule:** also refuse when the home, `instances/<name>/` or its `diagnostics/` grants any group or other permission (`mode & 0o077 != 0`; `strict::unix_read_verdict`). This is the Unix counterpart of the Windows read rule, so a pre-existing home cannot expose `events.ndjson` or `diagnostics/`.

The snapshot's `endpoint`, `pid` and `started_at` are the reference values for client server verification, so a client that skips this check verifies the server against values an attacker could have written.
an unstattable home (a path under a regular file) is a strict-modes refusal on Unix (`verify` exits 1 with the home pair, the frame verbs 21 with the instance pair)

a strict-modes check refuses a trusted path another user can write, a home, instance directory or `diagnostics/` another user can read (Unix any group or other bit; Windows an allow ACE granting a read right to another SID, inherit-only included) or a symlinked `diagnostics/` folder or file, in every process that reads a trusted file, before its first read or open under the home.

body_fields.why: The Windows owner-and-DACL strict-modes arm and its protected-DACL home creation must leave with the cfg(windows) code, its text staying as the unsupported OS's.
body_fields.quote: **Windows:** `%USERPROFILE%` inheritance (user + SYSTEM + Administrators) is accepted. A `--home` outside `%USERPROFILE%` gets an explicit protected user + SYSTEM DACL at creation (via windows-sys), or is refused if one cannot be set. **Windows strict-modes check:** at the same entry points as Unix, read the owner and DACL of the home,

body_fields.why: The ConPTY companions' strict-modes check in pin_companions must leave with sideload.rs and vendor/conpty/, with no Linux start path left reading a conpty/ folder.

body: **authentication-authorization (Windows IPC, SQOS client, Windows strict-modes) ↔ dependency-security**: removing the cfg(windows) IPC and DACL arms must remove their windows-sys use with the `[target.'cfg(windows)']` manifest entries and their deny.toml entries, while interprocess 2.4.4 stays the Unix IPC library (security-plan/authentication-authorization fct-y6zteyy6); `cargo deny check` stays green and the 0BSD per-crate exceptions for the crates interprocess pulls in are re-read against the Linux graph, never moved into `allow` (security-plan fct-32d4ty7r).

**authentication-authorization (client server verification) ↔ security-anti-patterns**: with the macOS carve-out gone, every Linux client seam must verify the server, euid, peer pid and start time, before any frame against a snapshot that passed the strict-modes check in the same process (security-plan/authentication-authorization fct-ju3c6nzj), and the frame-before-verification ban binds every client path, its carve-out borrowed by none (security-plan fct-6cauxi6n).

**authentication-authorization (refusals) ↔ error-handling**: the closed refusal causes the kept Unix arms emit, `socket-dir-refused`, `server-verify-failed` and `strict-modes-failed`, with exit 21 for the CLI and fail-open exit 0 for `hook` (security-plan/authentication-authorization fct-2pxk6g7w), stay the closed MCP `instance-unreachable` causes unchanged (security-plan fct-kulo4ws7).

**authentication-authorization ↔ security-anti-patterns (Universal)**: making the Unix peer-euid and strict-modes arms unconditional must add no environment, flag or feature seam that forces a refusing peer-euid decision or switches off the socket-directory, peer or home check (security-plan/authentication-authorization fct-ekk5s2bu) (security-plan fct-7ackeyph).

**authentication-authorization (strict-modes made unconditional) ↔ data-protection anti-patterns**: once the Windows arm leaves, no off-Unix `Ok(())` fallback of `check_socket_dir` or the strict-modes check survives as an unchecked path (security-plan/authentication-authorization fct-a6h3q7dw) (security-plan fct-fmxdaj54).

**authentication-authorization ↔ the plan body (expected amendment)**: the Windows ACL, named-pipe, SQOS and Windows strict-modes text stays in the security plan as the unsupported OS's text while the code leaves; the plan names the wrap's Linux-only amendment as expected and writes no master itself (security-plan/authentication-authorization fct-y6zteyy6) (security-plan fct-ju2d5wlo).

**authentication-authorization (witnesses) ↔ test-plan**: the cfg(windows) cases of the strict-modes and socket-directory witnesses leave with their gates and are re-pointed or retired in the OS-gated census, while every Linux case stays and is green (security-plan/authentication-authorization fct-65crhg3m) (security-plan/authentication-authorization fct-a2nznb7h).

IPC access control (Windows) — the listener gets an explicit protected DACL granting the user SID and SYSTEM only; the logon SID is deliberately not added, since the boundary v1 promises is the OS user; remote clients stay rejected, the first-pipe-instance behaviour is kept and the handle is not inheritable.

body_fields.why: The Windows `GetNamedPipeServerProcessId` arm and the macOS no-pid arm of the server-pid read leave. The Linux `SO_PEERCRED` pid read must stay the client's source of the observed server pid, and it must still write and log nothing.
body_fields.quote: The client reads the connected stream's peer pid through `Client::server_pid` / `TokioClient::server_pid` (`server_pid_of`, interprocess 2.4.4 `StreamCommon` `peer_creds().pid()`): on Linux `SO_PEERCRED`, on Windows `GetNamedPipeServerProcessId` on the SQOS-adopted client end, on macOS none. `SERVER_PID_REPORTED`, a `const bool` re-exported by `viola-channel`, is false on macOS. Reading the pid writes and logs nothing.

its `pid()` also the client's read of the serving process: Linux `SO_PEERCRED`, Windows `GetNamedPipeServerProcessId` on the SQOS-opened client end, none on macOS; its `euid()` the Unix read of the peer on both sides, the wrapper reading a client and a client reading the server, none on Windows)

body_fields.why: If the `cfg!(unix)` gate of `PEER_EUID_REPORTED` is made unconditional, the Linux client must still refuse a peer whose euid cannot be read, and the server must still drop a foreign-euid peer before any frame.
body_fields.quote: `peer_euid_admitted(observed, own, reported)` admits when not reported or when observed equals own (`!reported || observed == Some(own)`); `PEER_EUID_REPORTED` is `cfg!(unix)`, so a peer whose euid cannot be read is refused on Unix, and on Windows no euid is read and the DACL and the pid comparison stay the controls.
IPC server-side peer check (Unix) — on every accept, a peer whose euid differs from the server's is dropped before a frame is read.

body_fields.why: The macOS branch, where no pid is reported and the verdict is `Matches` with no comparison, leaves with the carve-out. The Linux client must keep comparing the peer pid and start time against the strict-checked snapshot, and must inherit no skipped check.
body_fields.quote: The verdict is the closed `viola_state::liveness::ServerVerdict { Matches, Mismatch, Unverifiable }`, from the pure `server_verdict` and the joined `verify_server` (the observed start time read from the OS through `process_start_time`). It compares the peer pid and that process's start time with the snapshot's `pid` and `started_at`, taken with the `endpoint` from one `read_snapshot_or_replay` call made after the instance's strict-modes check, only a parsed snapshot giving reference values (a replayed or absent one is no `LiveEndpoint` for the CLI frame verbs and `viola mcp`, and `NotSent::Unreachable`, failing open, for `viola hook`'s `connect`): the CLI frame verbs and `viola mcp` through `live_endpoint`, which returns `LiveEndpoint { endpoint, pid, started_at }` and runs its liveness pre-check before the server check; `viola hook` through its shared `connect`. Only `Matches` lets a frame be written. Where no peer pid is reported (`SERVER_PID_REPORTED` false, macOS) the verdict is `Matches` with no comparison.

IPC client-side server verification (anti-impersonation) — before the first frame of any method, the client runs the instance's strict-modes check, a refusal writing no frame and no line, and only then verifies the server against its one snapshot read: on Linux and Windows the connected peer's pid (Windows over an SQOS identification-level open) and that process's start time, a mismatch, a snapshot replayed from the log (no endpoint, pid or start time) or a check that cannot be made sending no frame, never falling back to a default connect; on Linux and macOS the client also checks the recorded endpoint's socket directory before the connect, a refusal reading `socket-dir-refused`, and past the connect admits only a peer of its own euid, an unreadable peer refused, a refusal reading `server-verify-failed`, each sending no frame; macOS compares no peer pid or start time, the named carve-out, owned by no route entry, so there `server-verify-failed` means an euid mismatch alone.

body_fields.why: The per-OS clauses of `link` and `unlink` collapse to Linux. On Linux they must still run the strict-modes check, then liveness, then the socket-directory check, connect, euid decision and server check, all before their one frame. The Unix strict-modes arm, if made unconditional, must refuse exactly what it refused before.
body_fields.quote: then `cmd::client::connect` before their one `link` / `unlink` frame: the socket-directory check on the recorded endpoint, the connect, the peer euid decision on Unix and, on Linux and Windows, the server check (macOS compares no pid or start time, the named carve-out).

a strict-modes check refuses a trusted path another user can write, a home, instance directory or `diagnostics/` another user can read (Unix any group or other bit; Windows an allow ACE granting a read right to another SID, inherit-only included) or a symlinked `diagnostics/` folder or file, in every process that reads a trusted file, before its first read or open under the home.

body_fields.why: The scope keeps every Linux exit code and closed word. A CLI frame verb's server or euid refusal must stay exit 21 with `server-verify-failed`, and a directory refusal exit 21 with `socket-dir-refused`, each with no frame, after the arms leave.
body_fields.quote: A CLI frame verb (`send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause`, `release`, `link`, `unlink`) meeting a mismatch, or a check that cannot be made, writes no frame and exits 21: under `--json` the document `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"server-verify-failed"}` on stdout with stderr empty; in human mode the `unable  <name>  instance-unreachable` line with the hint `the process on <name>'s endpoint is not its recorded wrapper; it was not contacted` last on stderr. A refused peer euid is this same mismatch, with the same document and hint. A socket-directory refusal, before the connect, writes no frame and exits 21: under `--json` the document `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"socket-dir-refused"}` on stdout with stderr empty; in human mode the same `unable` line with the hint of cause `socket-dir` last on stderr.

body_fields.why: `viola mcp`'s frame path must keep mapping each refused check to its closed `instance-unreachable` cause, with no frame and no line, when the peer and server checks lose their OS gates.
body_fields.quote: `viola mcp`'s `frame` maps a refused `check_instance` to `strict-modes-failed`, no `live_endpoint` to `without_endpoint`'s reading, a refused `check_endpoint_dir` after `live_endpoint` to `socket-dir-refused`, and a refused `peer_admitted` or a failed `server_verified` to `server-verify-failed`, each the `instance-unreachable` result with its cause in `detail`, with no frame and no line on any of them, `isError` the only record.

body_fields.why: The macos-latest cases leave with the macOS job, and the server-identity negatives' `#![cfg(not(target_os = "macos"))]` gate is a macOS gate that leaves too. The server-identity negatives must then run on ubuntu-latest.
body_fields.quote: On `macos-latest` a per-user socket directory at 0755 or a symlink to a 0700 one gives exit 21 on a frame verb, with `detail` `socket-dir-refused`, and the client euid read holds there. The server-identity negatives compile out on macOS, the named carve-out (below).

body_fields.why: The macOS carve-out leaves with its arms. Its `server_verdict_rows` row and its `NO_PEER_PID` census rows must be retired with the gates the edited census counted, and no other path may borrow the carve-out.
body_fields.quote:
The absent pid and start-time comparison of macOS is a named carve-out owned by no route entry: `server_verdict_rows` keeps its row and the server-identity negatives stay compiled out there.
- **Stack reference:** `server_verdict_rows`; `tests/security_negatives_server_identity.rs` (`#![cfg(not(target_os = "macos"))]`); `tests/contract_os_gated_tests.rs` (`GATES`, each test this carve-out keeps off macOS a row under its one reason `NO_PEER_PID`)

body_fields.quote: `tests/security_negatives_socket_dir.rs`, `#![cfg(unix)]`, holds the start, frame-verb and hook negatives over a 0755 directory and a symlink to a 0700 one, on `ubuntu-latest` and `macos-latest`, none on Windows.

body_fields.why: The scope bars any env, flag or feature seam that forces a refusing peer-euid decision. The foreign-euid and foreign-owner decisions stay held by injected values in their unit tests.
body_fields.quote: A foreign euid and a foreign owner are not driven by any test: one account can make no foreign peer, so those decisions are held by injected values, and no seam may be added to drive them.

body_fields.why: The `link`/`unlink` control tests carry Unix-only, Linux-and-Windows and Linux-and-macOS gates. Those gates must be removed or re-pointed so that every Linux control keeps its test.

body: **authentication-authorization (the macOS carve-out) ↔ test-plan (the OS-gated census)**: the carve-out's `NO_PEER_PID` rows in `tests/contract_os_gated_tests.rs` are retired with the macOS gates they counted (security-plan/authentication-authorization fct-ghctc7rk). The server-identity negatives then run ungated on ubuntu-latest (security-plan/authentication-authorization fct-ka73bihm), and the census, if it is re-pointed rather than retired, counts no gate that no longer exists.

**authentication-authorization (the peer-euid gate) ↔ security-anti-patterns (no seam switches off a control)**: making `PEER_EUID_REPORTED` unconditional keeps the unreadable-peer refusal (security-plan/authentication-authorization fct-zpaxdj2d), and no env, flag or feature seam may force or skip that decision (security-plan/authentication-authorization fct-efyzkncd) (security-plan fct-7ackeyph).

**authentication-authorization (the Windows witnesses) ↔ dependency-security (manifests and deny.toml)**: windows-sys and its `deny.toml` entries leave with the `[target.'cfg(windows)']` dependencies, together with the Windows witnesses that use them (security-plan/authentication-authorization fct-o3bl5eop). interprocess 2.4.4 and sysinfo 0.39.6 stay as the Linux peer-credential and start-time sources (security-plan fct-7nb5glkx). `cargo deny check` stays green with the licence allow list unchanged and the 0BSD exceptions re-read against the post-removal graph (security-plan fct-32d4ty7r).

**authentication-authorization (the closed refusals) ↔ error-handling (the closed instance-unreachable causes)**: the CLI's exit 21 documents and the MCP `instance-unreachable` causes `strict-modes-failed`, `socket-dir-refused` and `server-verify-failed` stay exactly as they are on Linux (security-plan/authentication-authorization fct-ybwsdbo3) (security-plan/authentication-authorization fct-6ntn52d2) (security-plan fct-kulo4ws7).

**authentication-authorization (Windows and macOS rows) ↔ the body (the expected security-plan amendment)**: the Windows ACL and named-pipe rows and the macOS carve-out rows are rewritten by the wrap's amendment, the Windows sections staying as unsupported-OS text (security-plan fct-kny6sapm) (security-plan fct-phspeqis). This chunk's plan names that amendment as expected and does not edit the master itself.

body_fields.why: The hook's instance check must keep running before any config, stdin or log use, and every failure must stay fail-open, when the strict-modes Unix arm loses its gate, as the scope keeps `hook`'s contract.
body_fields.quote: The event and dialog paths then canonicalise the instance directory and run the instance check (`canonical`, then `trusted`, in `src/cmd/hook.rs`: `viola_state::strict::check_instance`) before the diagnostics level and obs init: a `VIOLA_DIR` naming no existing instance directory, or an instance the check refuses, exits 0 at once with no `config.json` read, no stdin read, no line, no frame and no SessionEnd append.
every failure fails open (exit 0, no body); `budget.json` is written by `hook statusline` alone; the hidden capture arms read no `VIOLA_*`, open no channel and always exit 0.

body_fields.why: The frame verbs' client order must stay whole on Linux (socket-dir check, peer euid decision, server check, each before the frame) once the Windows and macOS arms of that order leave.
body_fields.quote: A passed check is followed by the liveness pre-check `live_endpoint` (the endpoint, `pid` and `started_at`), `check_endpoint_dir` on the parent of that endpoint (a refusal is exit 21, `socket-dir-refused`, no frame), the connect, on Unix the peer euid decision `peer_admitted` (a refusal reads `server-verify-failed`) and then, on Linux and Windows, the server check before the frame (IPC client-side server verification row).

then `canonical_home` applies `std::fs::canonicalize` when the path exists (on Windows a `\\?\C:\…` result is written back as `C:\…`, only the verbatim-drive prefix stripped; `\\?\UNC\…`, `\\?\Volume{…}\…` and `\\.\…` stay as given), while a path that does not exist keeps `std::path::absolute`'s spelling and nothing is created.

body_fields.why: The Unix R8 pass-list read in `src/run/env.rs`, whose Windows registry sibling leaves, must keep its whole rejection and its identity-floor rule if its gate is lifted.
body_fields.quote: `claude_env_keep` (the Unix R8 pass-list) is an array of at most 32 names, each matching `^CLAUDE[A-Z0-9_]*$`; a bad value is rejected WHOLE (never partly accepted) and reported as `parse-rejected`, and an identity-floor name in it has no effect (not an error).
an identity-floor name in `claude_env_keep` has no effect.

body_fields.why: The registry read leaves with its Windows arm, and the remaining Linux R8 rule must keep stripping every identity-floor name with no persistent-set source left.
body_fields.quote: `viola run` reads value NAMES only, never data, under `HKCU\Environment` and `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Environment`, into a bounded buffer; a missing key gives an empty set. The names only decide which inherited `CLAUDE*` names the R8 rule keeps, and an identity-floor name is stripped whatever the registry holds (operator ruling 2026-09-25, Decisions Log).

`viola run` reads value names only, never data, into a bounded buffer; they only decide which inherited `CLAUDE*` names the R8 rule keeps, and an identity-floor name is stripped whatever the registry holds.

body_fields.why: The pump-delay seam must stay compiled out of every release build and switch off nothing, as the task keeps both fake-agent seams and the Linux release job's feature refusal.
body_fields.quote: It is compiled out of every release build, is not a `VIOLA_*` variable, configures nothing, disables no control and widens no redaction (operator ruling 2026-09-27, Decisions Log).
compiled out of every release build, it configures nothing, disables no control and widens no redaction.

body_fields.why: The hook-panic seam must stay a closed value compiled out of release builds, since G2's one exemption kept on the Linux leg is its panic location.
body_fields.quote: Named in product source only in its own file; compiled out of every release build; not a `VIOLA_*` variable; configures nothing, disables no control and widens no redaction (the founder's ratification 2026-09-28, Decisions Log).

a closed value, panicking only on exactly `1` with a fixed ASCII payload, the hook still failing open; compiled out of every release build, it configures nothing, disables no control and widens no redaction.

body_fields.why: The Windows VT enable arm of `src/human/style.rs` leaves, and the Linux colour decision must keep the facts only compared, never echoed, reaching no log, error or refusal.
body_fields.quote: decided into the closed `Depth` (`Truecolor` · `Ansi256` · `Ansi16`) or none: none under `--json`, a passthrough role, `NO_COLOR` present (an empty value included), `TERM` exactly `dumb`, a non-terminal stdout, or a failed Windows VT enable (`GetConsoleMode`, then ` SetConsoleMode(mode | 0x0004) ` on stdout, the saved mode restored on drop; never viola-pty's `0x000c`). They decide only whether and how deep SGR bytes are written around rows already escaped; they reach no log line, error or refusal, are never set by viola, change no escaping or check, configure nothing, disable no control and widen no redaction.

body_fields.why: The strict-modes arm made unconditional must still run before every own-state read at every entry point, as the task requires it to refuse before the first read under the home.
body_fields.quote: **Integrity:** read only after the home strict-modes check, at every entry point.
read only after the home strict-modes check

body_fields.why: The feed-panic witness's OS-gated readings are re-cut by the removal, and on Linux it must keep reading the child's bytes and the absence of every panic word.
body_fields.quote: **Witness:** after a caught feed panic, `chaos_feed_panic_refuses_send_and_keeps_passthrough` reads the outer terminal: on Unix the child's bytes (`e4 b8 ad`) reach it, and on every OS none of `panic`, `parse-rejected`, `vt100`, `unable` or `hint:` appears on it; the Windows byte reading is owed to "Windows-only live measurements".

body_fields.why: The Windows PATHEXT search and the `.cmd`/`.bat` refusal leave with their arms while `viola run` must keep resolving its child itself and handing portable-pty an absolute path.
body_fields.quote: `viola run` resolves its child program itself and hands portable-pty an absolute path, because portable-pty 0.8.1's own Windows search tries the exact name first (it would hit the extensionless npm sh shim). On Windows the PATH search tries PATHEXT extensions only, never the bare name. A `claude.cmd`/`claude.bat` (case-insensitive) resolves to the fixed sibling `<dir>/node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-code/bin/claude.exe` when that file exists; the shim is never read or parsed.

Every other `.cmd`/`.bat`, including a `claude.cmd` without that sibling, is refused with the closed `AgentError::BatchScriptChild`: exit 1, no child spawned, `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:1, detail:"batch-script-child"}`, and the two fixed `unable:`/`hint:` stderr lines with no path or pid

body_fields.why: The shell-out's Unix gate is lifted, and it must keep exactly its `/bin/sh -c` one-argument form, its order after the instance check and its bounds, staying the only shell-out.

The arm's order: canonicalise the instance directory, the instance check, the log, stdin, the `budget.json` write, the snapshot read (`read_snapshot_or_replay`: a replayed snapshot carries no `statusline_command`, so nothing runs and nothing prints), the shell-out.
No log line and no span carries the command. Not controlled: what the command does; it runs as the user, as it does without viola. It remains the only shell-out.

the recorded command runs only from `hook statusline`, as `/bin/sh -c` with the command as one argument, never on Windows; its stdout is capped and printed byte for byte, never parsed, its wait bounded; no log line or span carries the command, and it remains the only shell-out.

body_fields.why: The DLL search restriction, the second statement of `main`, leaves with `sideload.rs` and `src/conpty.rs`, and no Linux role may keep calling into the removed sideload code.

body_fields.quote: A `viola mcp` frame tool runs the instance's strict-modes check (`check_instance`) before its liveness pre-check; a refused check, like a snapshot that is replayed or absent (no live endpoint), sends no frame and returns the unreachable result: `isError` `instance-unreachable`, text `refused: instance-unreachable`, and no log line, `detail` reading `strict-modes-failed` for a refused check and, with no live endpoint, `viola_state::liveness::without_endpoint`'s cause: `instance-dead` for an instance directory, `unwrapped-name` for anything else. With a live endpoint it then runs `check_endpoint_dir` on that endpoint's parent: a refusal sends no frame and returns the same unreachable result, `detail` `socket-dir-refused`, and no log line.

body_fields.why: the server-side peer euid drop is a Unix arm the task requires to stay whole on Linux, so a refused stream must still be dropped on the accept thread before any frame with no reply, line or terminal byte.
body_fields.quote: A stream `accept_loop` refuses by `admitted(peer_euid_of(stream))` is dropped on the accept thread, before its worker thread and before any frame: the peer reads end-of-file, and the wrapper writes no reply, no line and nothing on the terminal, there being no frame to key a `channel-response` on.

body_fields.why: the CLI's strict-modes refusal rides the Unix strict-modes arm the chunk keeps or makes unconditional once the Windows owner-and-DACL arm leaves, and it must keep exit 21, the same document and no open or line under the home.
body_fields.quote: CLI `send` · `wait` · `last` · `answer` · `pause` · `release`, as `link` / `unlink`, run the instance's strict-modes check (`client::refuse_untrusted`: `check_instance` on the home and `instances/<name>`) before any frame: a refusal exits 21, prints the instance pair (`human::instance_state_pair`) through `human::refuse`, or under `--json` exactly `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"strict-modes-failed"}`, opens nothing under the home and writes no line.

body_fields.why: the removal must leave exit 21's closed six-cause set and both clients' documents unchanged on Linux, with no cause word lost with a removed arm and no Windows- or ConPTY-only variant's removal letting a path or upstream text into an external error.
body_fields.quote: Exit 21's `detail` is a closed set of six causes, `strict-modes-failed` · `instance-dead` · `unwrapped-name` · `endpoint-lost` · `server-verify-failed` · `socket-dir-refused`: the CLI's `--json` document reads `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"<cause>"}`, and MCP's `isError` result the same less `v`, its text `refused: instance-unreachable`.

MCP `isError` results carry only the `structuredContent` codes from Conventions (`refusal`/`detail`, or `error: instance-unreachable | wrapper-fault | invalid-params` — `instance-unreachable` with `detail` its closed cause, `strict-modes-failed` · `instance-dead` · `unwrapped-name` · `endpoint-lost` · `server-verify-failed` · `socket-dir-refused`,

The `Display` impls on `PtyError` (hand-written) and on `AgentError`, `ChannelError`, `StateError`, `PinError`, `StampsError`, `StampsReadError`, `Refused`, `McpError` and `ServeError` (`thiserror`) use fixed messages. Variant fields that hold paths or payloads are excluded from `Display`.

body_fields.why: with the macOS carve-out gone, a refused peer euid must still read `server-verify-failed` through each of its three client types on Linux, never gaining a word of its own.
body_fields.quote: A peer euid that `peer_admitted` refuses has no word of its own: it is `CallError::ServerUnverified` in `src/cmd/client.rs`, `NotSent::ServerUnverified` in `src/cmd/hook.rs` and `UnreachableCause::ServerVerify` in `crates/viola-mcp/src/tools.rs`, each reading `server-verify-failed`.

body_fields.why: `socket-dir-refused` on the CLI frame verbs rides the Unix socket-directory check the task keeps whole, and must keep exit 21, `during` `connect`, its hint cause and its one WARN `process-exit` with no `channel-request`.
body_fields.quote: `viola_core::UnreachableCause::SocketDir`, its word `socket-dir-refused`, has no `RefusalReason`; on a CLI frame verb it is `CallError::SocketDirRefused` to `Unreachable::SocketDir`: exit 21, `during` `connect`, hint cause `socket-dir`, one `process-exit` at WARN and no `channel-request`.

body: **error-handling ↔ authentication-authorization**: the macOS carve-out leaves with its arms, so on Linux every client path (hook, MCP, CLI) must refuse as `server-verify-failed` on an euid mismatch, a peer that is not the recorded wrapper by pid and start time, or a check that cannot be made, sending no frame first; no client path may inherit the carve-out's skipped pid and start-time check (security-plan/error-handling fct-2qzjtoe6) (security-plan/error-handling fct-pfehx2bz) (security-plan fct-phspeqis) (security-plan fct-6cauxi6n).

**error-handling ↔ input-validation**: the hook's fail-open contract (exit 0, no body, empty stderr) must hold for every refusal the Linux arms keep, the socket-directory, server-verify and strict-modes refusals included, and the ungated statusline path must run no command from a replayed snapshot (security-plan/error-handling fct-io4zn2wb) (security-plan/error-handling fct-wandj5yh) (security-plan fct-u7v2p5mv) (security-plan fct-2fgozo5r).

**error-handling ↔ data-protection**: the Unix strict-modes arm, made unconditional when the Windows owner-and-DACL arm leaves, must produce the same `strict-modes-failed` refusals as before (CLI exit 21, MCP `isError`, hook exit 0), each before any frame and before the first read under the home (security-plan/error-handling fct-uv5qlev7) (security-plan/error-handling fct-tukgmehf) (security-plan fct-jya3vgt6).

**error-handling ↔ bootstrap-phases (error-sanitization-wire)**: removing ConPTY- or Windows-only error variants must leave every product error `Display` a fixed message that carries no path or upstream text, and the closed exit-21 cause set unchanged (security-plan/error-handling fct-au76dwrt) (security-plan fct-scytqusw) (security-plan fct-y26eifc2).

**error-handling ↔ security-anti-patterns**: every Linux refusal these entities name must still go only to automation and never block the human, the server-side euid drop writing nothing on the terminal (security-plan/error-handling fct-3t6spjp3) (security-plan fct-ciublye4).

body_fields.why: the Unix socket-directory check, kept whole and possibly ungated by this chunk, must keep refusals that name only the parsed name, with no path, pid or uid.
body_fields.quote: The socket-directory refusal names only the parsed `ViolaName`, and its lines hold no path, pid or uid.

body_fields.why: the socket-dir-refused refusal of run and revive's start is a closed Linux refusal that must act exactly as before once its Unix gate is gone.
body_fields.quote: `viola run` and `viola revive`'s start, before any snapshot, child or `Server::bind`, refuse a socket directory through `refused_with` and `refuse_socket_dir`: exit 1 and one `process-exit` of `detail` `socket-dir-refused`, a step with no span.
`instance-unreachable` with `detail` its closed cause, `strict-modes-failed` · `instance-dead` · `unwrapped-name` · `endpoint-lost` · `server-verify-failed` · `socket-dir-refused`
`hook` never writes to stderr and never exits non-zero: a security check failing in `hook` still ends in exit 0 with no body, so the dialog renders for the human

body_fields.why: the home strict-modes refusal must keep its Unix behaviour, exit codes and silent refusal once its Windows half leaves and the Unix arm is made unconditional.
body_fields.quote: `viola run` and `viola revive`'s start run the home tree's strict-modes check (`check_home_tree`, over the instance and the pinned copy's key) before the wrapper log opens: a refusal exits 1 with the home pair for a home-level refusal or the instance pair for an instance-level one, and opens no log, writes no line and starts no child (`revive --json` prints `strict-modes-failed`). `viola verify` runs the check on the home, `ledger/`, `bin/` and `plugin/` before its `cli` log, and a refusal there exits 1 with the home pair, no step line, no summary and no line; `update_stamps`'s `StampsError::StrictModes` exits 1 with the home pair, no step line and no summary, and its `process-exit`, under a parsed `VIOLA_NAME`, carries `strict-modes-failed`. On Unix a home under a regular file (unstattable) is such a refusal (the frame verbs: exit 21, the instance pair); on Windows that path stats `NotFound` and the `cli` catch-site line stands.

body_fields.why: the diagnostics strict-modes check must keep failing open on a symlink or a mode another user may use when its Unix arm is ungated and its Windows grant arm leaves.
body_fields.quote: A `diagnostics/` folder, role file or detail file that fails `strict::check_diagnostics` (a symbolic link, or a mode or grant another user may use) is a failed open, checked before anything is narrowed: the role writer ends at `std::io::sink` and the detail line is dropped.

body_fields.quote: `Refused::NotADirectory` carries the fixed `Display` message `a trusted state path is not a directory`; `check_socket_dir` returns it for a path that is no directory, `Refused::Symlink` for a symlink and `Refused::Unreadable` for an unstattable path.

body_fields.quote: `viola_state::stamps::StampsError` (`StrictModes` · `State`, the error `update_stamps` returns) and `viola_state::pin::PinError::StrictModes` carry fixed `Display` messages with no path or payload: `the capability stamps failed the strict-modes check`, a write failure its own fixed message, and `the pinned copy failed the strict-modes check`; `run` maps `PinError::StrictModes` to the `sideload_fallback` outcome `strict-modes-failed`.

body_fields.why: the .cmd/.bat refusal AgentError::BatchScriptChild leaves with the Windows arms, and resolve_program's remaining refusal must keep its fixed message in both homes.
body_fields.quote: `resolve_program` returns `Result<PathBuf, AgentError>` in `viola_agent_claude` and in the root wrapper `src/run/mod.rs`, its refusals `AgentError::BatchScriptChild` and `AgentError::ProgramNotFound`, each a fixed message; `src/cmd/revive.rs`'s private `Refusal` is another type.

body_fields.why: the error-body enumeration must name exactly the writers left after the removal and keep failing on an unnamed writer or an interpolating message, as the witness of the fixed messages the chunk re-asserts.
body_fields.quote: `tests/contract_error_bodies.rs`, carrying `andromeda:walks-tree`, enumerates every error body with its writer and witness (`CLI_DOCUMENTS`, `MCP_RESULTS`, `CHANNEL_FAULTS`, with `NOT_ERROR_BODIES` and `PLUMBING` the named exclusions); `product_error_writers_are_each_named` fails on an unnamed product error writer and `thiserror_messages_interpolate_nothing` on an interpolating `thiserror` message.

body_fields.why: the exit-21 and exit-1 cause table must keep witnessing the typed exit codes the chunk re-asserts unchanged on Linux, with no cause added or lost by the removal.
