**error-handling ↔ data-protection**: the home and diagnostics strict-modes checks, their Windows owner-and-DACL arm removed (security-plan fct-jya3vgt6), must keep refusing exactly what the Unix arm refused, with the same exit pairs, silent refusal and failed-open diagnostics (security-plan/error-handling fct-j463drna) (security-plan/error-handling fct-wyrvqwn5) (security-plan/error-handling fct-ttxl4mzv).

**error-handling ↔ input-validation**: the `.cmd`/`.bat` refusal leaves with the Windows child-resolution arm (security-plan fct-sgmmo3ki), so `AgentError::BatchScriptChild` goes with it while `ProgramNotFound` keeps its fixed message (security-plan/error-handling fct-zu3fn6nz), and the thiserror census and error-body enumeration must be re-recorded to the surviving set (security-plan/error-handling fct-hzzqncjb) (security-plan/error-handling fct-syp3b7yx).

**error-handling ↔ security-anti-patterns**: removing ConPTY- or Windows-only variants must let no path or upstream text into an external error (security-plan fct-6xxq3ubv) (security-plan/error-handling fct-g4i32qdx), and the `sideload_fallback` outcome `strict-modes-failed` is decided as text naming removed code or kept as a Linux closed word (security-plan fct-my3j53so).

**error-handling ↔ the body (unchanged Linux contracts)**: the typed exit codes stay witnessed by the cause table (security-plan/error-handling fct-ticjysfg), and `hook` keeps exit 0, no body and no stderr on any security-check failure (security-plan fct-r24nqlwe).

body_fields.why: removing the Windows pid read and the macOS carve-out must leave every Linux client path (CLI verbs, `hook`, `mcp`) verifying the server's euid, pid and start time against a strict-checked `snapshot.json` before any frame, inheriting no skipped check.
body_fields.quote: NEVER write any channel frame (`send`, `answer`, `hook.dialog`, `wait`/`last`, `pause`/`release`, `link`/`unlink`, and `hook.event` notifications, which carry prompt and reply text) before verifying the server's pid (Windows: the connected stream's peer pid, interprocess `peer_creds().pid()`, which calls `GetNamedPipeServerProcessId` on the SQOS-adopted client end) or euid + pid (Linux/FreeBSD `peer_creds()`; the client-side euid check, `peer_admitted(client.server_euid())` at the three client seams, before the server verification) plus sysinfo start time against `snapshot.json` (on macOS, where `peer_creds()` gives no pid: euid + the verified 0700 socket directory only, per the recorded known gap; the euid check is never skipped), and NEVER take those reference values (`endpoint`, `pid`, `started_at`) from a `snapshot.json` that has not passed the strict-modes check in the same process.

NEVER write any channel frame before verifying the server against a `snapshot.json` that passed the strict-modes check in the same process (the euid check never skipped), except the named carve-out: macOS's pid and start-time check (no peer pid), owned by no route entry, its euid and verified socket-directory checks standing; no other frame or process may borrow it.

NEVER rely on the socket file's 0600 mode as the only Unix control: `unix(7)` says socket permissions may be ignored. NEVER set it with `ListenerOptionsExt::mode`: it returns `Unsupported` on macOS, which fails the bind; chmod after the bind instead.
NEVER enable rmcp's `transport-streamable-http-server` or `auth` features.

NEVER create `~/.viola/`, `--home` or any file under it with the default umask. Directories are 0700 and files 0600 (`OpenOptionsExt::mode`); the only exception is the pinned `bin/<version>-<hash>/viola` at 0700, and NEVER make it group- or world-writable. On Windows, NEVER accept a `--home` outside `%USERPROFILE%` without an explicit protected user + SYSTEM DACL, and NEVER skip the Windows owner + DACL strict-modes check at startup (`#[cfg(windows)]` must not return `Ok(())` unchecked)
NEVER run `statusline_command` from a `snapshot.json` whose home or instance directory fails the strict-modes check. Write access there equals code execution.

NEVER reuse an existing `bin/<version>-<hash>/viola(.exe)` without re-hashing it (SHA-256, truncated) against `<hash>`, NEVER derive `<hash>` from a non-cryptographic hash (FNV, `DefaultHasher`), and NEVER reuse existing `plugin/` files without rewriting them. NEVER load or launch a `bin/<version>-<hash>/conpty/` companion without its full SHA-256 re-hash against the compiled pin through a `FILE_SHARE_READ`-only handle held until the spawn, and NEVER overwrite or delete a companion that fails it (left as found; the child runs on the inbox ConPTY).
NEVER spawn a `.cmd`/`.bat` PTY child through portable-pty. Resolve to a real `.exe` (portable-pty 0.8.1 bypasses std's BatBadBut escaping).
NEVER write to stderr from `viola hook`, and NEVER exit non-zero from it, including on security-check failures.
NEVER spawn a `.cmd`/`.bat` PTY child through portable-pty.
NEVER load or launch a `bin/<version>-<hash>/conpty/` companion without its full SHA-256 re-hash against the compiled pin through a `FILE_SHARE_READ`-only handle held until the spawn

NEVER create `~/.viola/`, `--home` or any file under it with the default umask. Directories are 0700 and files 0600 (`OpenOptionsExt::mode`); the only exception is the pinned `bin/<version>-<hash>/viola` at 0700, and NEVER make it group- or world-writable.
NEVER reuse an existing `bin/<version>-<hash>/viola(.exe)` without re-hashing it (SHA-256, truncated) against `<hash>`, NEVER derive `<hash>` from a non-cryptographic hash (FNV, `DefaultHasher`)
NEVER create `diagnostics/` files readable by other users.
NEVER expose absolute paths in any external error.

body_fields.why: the `HOST_SCRATCH = cfg!(windows)` guard and wipe leave with the Windows arms, so on Linux the harness must still touch no scratch, never wipe the operator's mutation `TMPDIR`, and keep the no-fallback, no-printed-path ban wherever the `--package` arm and the git-history base survive.
body_fields.quote: NEVER fall back to `%TEMP%` or the repository, and NEVER print the path. The guard and the wipe run only on a Windows host (`HOST_SCRATCH = cfg!(windows)`); elsewhere the harness touches no scratch, and the Linux dev host's same-named NOCOW `TMPDIR` for mutation runs is the operator's, never wiped by the harness.

NEVER let `run --mutants` wipe any directory except the Windows host mutation scratch `<repo parent>/viola-mutants-scratch`, guarded by its exact final component; NEVER re-create it without owner-only permissions, loosen the strict-modes check for it, fall back to `%TEMP%` or the repository, or print the path.

body_fields.why: the msrv fix edits the two e2e-home backing cases and the free-space floor message, so the cases must decide on a test-controlled free-space figure while the keepers keep refusing a link-target, a group/other bit and a backing below the 9 GiB floor with a fixed message naming no path, creating 0700 and removing nothing.
body_fields.quote: The two keepers (`prepare_home_base` in `tests/support/home.rs`, `Workspace::ensure_e2e_home` in the harness) NEVER follow a linked base unless its target is absolute and one `lstat` of it reads a real directory with no group or other bit; a target that is itself a link is refused, so is a backing whose filesystem reads less than the 9 GiB headroom floor free (`statvfs`), and a refusal is a fixed message that names no path (the headroom one holds the two counts). They create the target with mode 0700 through the directory builder (never a chmod after, never a parent) and remove nothing. Ownership is not read separately: the `tempdir_in` that follows succeeds in an owner-only directory only for its owner. `viola` itself never reads or writes the backing by that name, and no CI runner has the link.

NEVER let a test-side removal under `target/e2e-home` take anything but a dir the test side itself created; its two keepers NEVER follow a linked base unless its target is absolute and an owner-only real directory, create the target 0700 and remove nothing; `viola` itself never reads or writes the backing by that name.

body_fields.why: the relied set's Windows arm (`/21`, status line unwrapped) leaves with every `cfg(windows)` arm, and the Linux relied set must stay the full `/24` so a non-`null` decision still flows only when every relied row passes.
body_fields.quote: a stamp is read over the relied set (`LedgerRow::relied()`, counter `/24` on Unix; on Windows, where the status line is not wrapped, the first eighteen, `resume-session`, `agents-join` and `local-command-compact`, counter `/21`), so a non-`null` decision flows only when every relied row passes

NEVER answer a `hook.dialog` with a non-`null` decision unless `ledger/stamps.json` holds a `viola verify` stamp for the child's CLI version on which every relied ledger row passes, and NEVER let any process other than `viola verify` write `ledger/stamps.json`: a stamp is what switches on dialog answering, PermissionRequest `allow` included.

body_fields.why: the scope's boundaries name this invariant, so un-gating the `cfg(unix)` peer-euid arms and removing the other OSes' tests must add no seam that forces a refusing peer-euid decision, the decisions staying proven over injected values.
body_fields.quote: NEVER add an env, flag or feature seam to force a refusing peer-euid decision: one account can make no foreign peer, so the decisions are proven over injected values (`peer_euid_admitted(observed, own, reported)`, and the wrapper's private `serve_admitting(dispatch, admitted)` over an injected `Admission`), and each client seam's `peer_admitted` wiring (`cmd::client::connect`, `cmd::hook::connect`, `viola-mcp`'s `frame`) stays the named weakest proof, read only through a run's forced refusal, which no committed test repeats.

body: **Security anti-patterns (frame-before-verification ban) ↔ Authentication & Authorization (client server verification)**: once the Windows pid read and the macOS carve-out leave, the Linux client must keep the socket-directory check before connect (`socket-dir-refused`), the euid admission and the pid plus start-time check past it (`server-verify-failed`), each sending no frame, and the carve-out's text is the wrap's amendment, never a skipped check the Linux path inherits (security-plan/security-anti-patterns fct-izf47ccx) (security-plan fct-phspeqis)

**Security anti-patterns (`run --mutants` scratch) ↔ Dependency Security (CI integration)**: `windows-mutants.yml` and its contract test leave whole, and `run --mutants`' base stays derived from git history with `AGENT_RUN_CHUNK_BASE` only a local override; the scratch ban's Windows text becomes the wrap's unsupported-OS amendment (security-plan/security-anti-patterns fct-f5tdilgi) (security-plan fct-lpbl5pyp) (security-plan fct-npplilir)

body:
Makes viola Linux-only. It first sets the tag multi-os-final on the last commit that still holds the three-OS code and pushes it to origin before any removal commit. Take-up re-reads that no multi-os-* tag stands, locally or on origin.
Removes every cfg(windows) and cfg(target_os = "macos") arm with its tests and fixtures, the four Windows-only files (1 146 lines, re-read at take-up), vendor/conpty/, and the cfg(windows) target dependencies in the manifests along with their deny.toml entries. A cfg(unix) arm whose only sibling is gone loses its gate.
Removes the Windows and macOS CI jobs from ci.yml (test, lint, perf, release) and from nightly.yml, deletes windows-mutants.yml, and drops any pre-push or harness step that runs only for those OSes. The census of OS-gated tests is re-pointed or retired.
Fixes the msrv failure of ci#41930831242: the two viola-e2e e2e-home backing cases must decide on a free-space figure the test controls, never the host's. No Linux behaviour, exit code, closed word or wire contract changes.
Acceptance: every gate is green on Linux, no Windows or macOS job remains in any workflow, no cfg(windows) or target_os = "macos" remains in the tree, and the tag resolves on origin. The plan names the masters' Linux-only amendments as expected; the wrap writes them.

body: The recovery tag multi-os-final goes on the last three-OS commit and is pushed to origin before any removal commit. Its resolving on origin is part of the acceptance.

IPC access control and anti-impersonation. The Windows arms leave: the listener's protected DACL, the SQOS client open and the named-pipe server-pid read. The Unix arms must stay whole and act on Linux exactly as before: the per-user 0700 socket directory checked before bind and connect, chmod 0600 after bind, the server-side peer euid drop, and the client's server verification (peer pid and start time, euid, socket-dir check, and the closed refusals server-verify-failed and socket-dir-refused).

The macOS carve-out (no peer pid or start-time comparison, server-verify-failed meaning an euid mismatch alone) and its code leave with the macOS arms. The remaining Linux client may not inherit any skipped check from it, and the frame-before-verification ban still binds every client path.

Strict-modes checks on the viola home (owner, mode bits, no symlinked diagnostics). The Windows owner-and-DACL arm leaves, and the Unix arm, if made unconditional, must keep refusing exactly what it refused before, in every process, before the first read under the home.

cfg(unix) arms made unconditional. This covers the statusline shell-out (/bin/sh -c, the only shell-out), the Unix-only settings override written only for a pinned path of plain characters, and the scan class for non-0600 diagnostics files. Each keeps its Linux behaviour and gains no new reach.

Windows-only input and spawn controls leave with their arms: the registry read of persistent-environment names, the .cmd/.bat refusal with the claude shim resolution, and the DLL search restriction called as the second statement of main in every role. Whether text naming them goes is decided item by item, under the P4 rule for text naming removed code.

The sideloaded ConPTY companions (owner/DACL check, full SHA-256 re-hash by absolute path, silent fallback to the inbox ConPTY) leave with sideload.rs and vendor/conpty/. The pinned binary's own SHA-256 re-hash and the plugin rewrite at every start stay as they are.

The vendored ConPTY gate: scripts/conpty-vendor.sh parses its four pins from src/conpty.rs, and the windows-2025-only test step ConPTY vendor verification runs its --verify and --probe. Both lose their subject when src/conpty.rs and vendor/conpty/ go.

Dependency audit after the manifest edits. cargo deny check must stay green over all four check families. The licence allow list stays exactly MIT, Apache-2.0, Zlib and Unicode-3.0, with 0BSD admitted only by the per-crate exceptions. The bans.features entries for rmcp and serde_json, the C-crate bans, deny-sync.toml, channel-tokio-free.sh and deny-probes.sh all stay live. The single RUSTSEC-2017-0008 ignore stays tied to the portable-pty pin.

Pinning after the removal. Cargo.lock stays committed and every build stays --locked. [workspace.dependencies] keeps pinning every remaining third-party version (portable-pty =0.8.1). The lockfile floors stay in force: rmcp >=3.4.1 and bytes >=1.11.1.

Workflow hardening on every edited workflow: workflow-level permissions {} and job-level contents: read, actions pinned by full SHA with a version comment, actions/checkout with persist-credentials: false, no github.event value inside run:, matrix values only through env:, and toolchains from rustup steps. zizmor .github/workflows/ on the ubuntu leg must still pass. No concurrency block is added.

The test job's tool: line in ci.yml is the version source that viola-harness pre-push's tools stage parses (the cargo-nextest, cargo-mutants and cargo-llvm-cov pins). It must survive the matrix removal intact and readable.

The perf job's per-OS uploads (perf-<os>, diag-perf-<os>, secret-scan-perf-<os>) and the harness-<os> upload shrink to the Linux leg. Each stays gated on its secret-scan passing, and target/agent-run/chunk.diff stays skipped and never uploaded.

The release job, run through scripts/release-check.sh, keeps its Linux leg: its --probe reads 5/5 refused with a clean control, and it refuses any executable other than viola and any artifact built with a test-only feature (test-support, fake-agent).

nightly.yml keeps, on Linux, the weekly cargo deny check advisories over the root lockfile and over fuzz/Cargo.lock, and the fuzz job with its upload of crash inputs on failure. The fuzz/ test-only exemption is unchanged.
The msrv job (rustup toolchain install 1.96, selected by RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=1.96) must be green. Its red subject is the e2e-home free-space floor in the viola-e2e harness.

The e2e-home keepers in crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/mod.rs: a test-side removal under target/e2e-home takes only a directory the test side created; the keepers never follow a linked base unless its target is absolute and an owner-only real directory, create the target 0700, and remove nothing; viola itself never reads or writes the backing. The fix must leave all of this intact.

run --mutants and its Windows host scratch guard (viola-mutants-scratch, owner-only, never falling back to %TEMP% or the repository, path never printed). Its dispatch-only workflow and its contract test leave. The --package arm and the base taken from git history keep the same ban wherever that code survives.

The unchanged Linux contracts. The typed exit codes stay 0, 1, 2, 10–14, 20 and 21. hook exits 0 with no body and no stderr, a failing security check included. Security refusals go only to automation, never to the human. The NEVER-log floor stays as it is.

No environment variable, flag or feature seam may force a refusing peer-euid decision or switch off any control. The two fake-agent test seams stay compiled out of release builds, and no new seam or environment read is added without a Decisions Log entry.

Product error Display impls (PtyError and the thiserror enums) keep their fixed messages. Removing ConPTY- or Windows-only variants must not let a path or upstream text into an external error, and the closed instance-unreachable causes stay as they are.

Expected security-plan amendment, written by the wrap: the CI/CD line's three-OS matrix, the ConPTY dependency and vendor rows, and the per-OS CI job rows become Linux-only. The Windows ACL and named-pipe sections stay, as the text for an unsupported OS.
The G2 zero-panics gate keeps exactly one exemption, the FAKE_AGENT_HOOK_PANIC seam's panic_location, and its --probe runs before every G2 check.

body_fields.convention: each CI job or step added or kept holds job-level contents: read under workflow permissions {}, uses SHA-pinned actions with a version comment and checkout with persist-credentials: false, and passes event or matrix values only through env:
each scan-gated upload in CI waits for the secret-scan step (if: always()) to pass, and no scan ever prints or writes the matched bytes
each test runs against its own --home, and every child of the pre-push gate runs under env -i with exactly HOME and PATH, so no host value crosses into a child
each test seam or environment read lives only under a test-only feature compiled out of release builds, switches off no control, and any new one needs its own Decisions Log entry
each log, diagnostics or error line obeys the NEVER-log floor: no user content, tool input, absolute path or stripped CLAUDE* value outside diagnostics/, and diagnostics files are 0600
each fixture or test input is synthetic, with no real prompts, home paths or usernames committed
each new G2 zero-panics exemption needs its own Decisions Log entry

MCP tool-input handling and the structuredContent refusal codes. No MCP handler or tool schema changes.
The dialog-answering gate: ledger/stamps.json stamps from viola verify, read_stamps_strict, the unverified-cli gate and the closed behavior enum. The chunk answers no dialog and writes no stamp.

viola verify's live probes and their accepted risks and residuals: Runs B to E, the scratch footer reading, the live plugin-install round, the dev-host prerequisite for the real-CLI probe, and the --record fixture scrub. The chunk runs 0 live sessions.

v1.x release prerequisites: dist with attestations and signing, cargo-auditable with cargo audit bin, self_update with signatures, and the rust-cache ban in a release workflow. v1 has no release workflow.
The human terminal's stdin classifier (the closed non-editing list) and bracketed-paste breakout. No PTY input path changes on Linux.
The vt100 feed under catch_unwind and the poisoning of the screen model.
Harness prefixes, screen signatures and local-command lists built only from compiled ledger rows.
Unwrapped-session list rows: escape_row, and a claude agents --json row name never used as a ViolaName or target.
revive's session-id argv built by resume_args, and the no-session refusal.
The driver-originated release guard (release-from-driver), the from param never being an identity, and the accepted risk of driver prompt injection.
events.ndjson retention, the accepted risk to local availability, and the omitted key management.
Secret rotation cadence and the v1.x signing credentials counted as secrets. No secret enters the repo or CI.
The security tier, data classification and compliance triggers of the threat-model summary. The chunk changes none of them.

body:
Makes viola Linux-only: removes every cfg(windows) and cfg(target_os = "macos") arm with its tests and fixtures, the four Windows-only files, vendor/conpty and the Windows target dependencies with their deny.toml entries; a cfg(unix) arm whose only sibling left loses its gate.
Removes the Windows and macOS jobs of ci.yml (test, lint, perf, release) and nightly.yml, windows-mutants.yml whole, and any pre-push or harness step that runs only for those OSes; the census of OS-gated tests is re-pointed or retired with the gates it counted.
First sets and pushes the tag multi-os-final on the last three-OS commit, before any removal commit; re-reads at take-up that no multi-os-* tag stands and that the four files hold 1 146 lines.
Fixes the two viola-e2e harness cases that read the host's real free space against the 9216 MiB e2e-home floor, so they decide on a figure the test controls and msrv is green again (ci#41930831242, abf00915).
Changes no Linux behaviour; acceptance is every gate green on Linux, no Windows or macOS job in any workflow, no Windows or macOS cfg left in the tree, and the tag resolving on origin; the test-plan's 3-OS CI matrix and per-OS legs are named as expected amendments the wrap writes.

body: The CI matrix of section 9: windows-2025, macos-latest and ubuntu-latest with fail-fast false shrinks to ubuntu-latest, with the per-OS test, lint and perf jobs and their per-OS artifact names (harness-, diag-, junit-, perf-, diag-perf-, secret-scan- by matrix.os).

The build failure conditions worded per OS: a test failure or coverage breach on any of the 3 OSes, and the ConPTY vendor errors on windows-2025 (scripts/conpty-vendor.sh --verify and its --probe), which leave with vendor/conpty and the Windows job.

The audit's Windows mutation leg: the dispatch-only, report-only windows-mutants.yml named in sections 9 and 10, tests/contract_windows_mutation_scope.rs, and the Windows-host mutation scratch directory beside the repository named in the agent-runnable invariants.
nightly.yml: its Windows and macOS jobs leave, while the time-boxed cargo fuzz runs and the weekly advisories over the root and fuzz lockfiles stay on ubuntu.

The multi-os-compat coverage trigger and its OS-branch tests (named pipe vs Unix socket, ConPTY vs openpty, Windows DACL and strict-modes vs Unix modes, macOS euid and dir-only server verification), and the Test-Relevant Convention that every OS branch is tested on its own runner, retired with the gates.

The harness shim pair of section 3: scripts/agent-run.sh and scripts/agent-run.ps1 as identical thin shims on all 3 OSes; only Windows CI steps run the .ps1 (the two pwsh shim steps and the windows-mutants step), and CLAUDE.md, the harness letters and health check 13 name the sh/ps1 pair.

The ConPTY sideload and its test carve-outs: tests/conpty_sideload.rs (a companion another user may write leaves the child on the inbox ConPTY with sideload_fallback strict-modes-failed), the seed_conpty seeding of Windows x64 homes in the integration lifecycle and seed strategies, the DA1 answer under the sideloaded ConPTY, and the root tests' children hosted on the sideloaded ConPTY.

Windows DACL and SDDL tests: the icacls set and read-back in tests/support/home.rs, the pipe DACL read in canonical form, the synthetic SDDL descriptor stubs for foreign-owner SIDs and non-persistent-ACL volumes, Windows strict-modes over real grants on windows-2025, the read-granted-home board scan case, and a Windows --home outside the profile given a protected DACL.

Windows channel and process tests: the named-pipe listener rejecting remote clients and denying an anonymous open, client SQOS at the identification level, Windows handle non-inheritance, and the windows-sys TerminateProcess fallback of viola-pty, the cfg(windows) path of its unit cases.

The .cmd / .bat PTY child refusal (run exit 1 on the windows runner, the chaos suite's .cmd case and the exit-cause matrix's .cmd human pair): whether its code and text name a removed arm is listed by P3 and decided by P4.

macOS carve-outs: the units compiled out on macOS (the two real-cargo-mutants harness tests and the server check's captured-span cases), server_verdict_rows comparing no peer pid on macOS, tests/security_negatives_server_identity.rs on Linux and Windows and tests/security_negatives_socket_dir.rs on Linux and macOS, the macOS 26 arm64 runner, and the untestable zone of macOS local runs.

cfg(unix) arms made unconditional where their only sibling left: the statusline pass-through on Unix only, the instance settings.json written on Unix, claude_env_keep on Unix, diagnostics 0600 on Unix, and the fake agent's per-command process group and SIGHUP-ignoring exit on Unix, each keeping its Linux behaviour.

The test-scope entities and surfaces whose text names Windows or macOS code: viola-channel's Windows listener asserted on test (windows-2025), viola-state's and config state's Windows DACL limitation, the R8 strip's Windows registry Environment names and the identity floor measured on the Windows host, hook statusline's Windows arm that runs no command, and library tests running on all three CI OSes.

OS text without a cfg gate that the removal may leave naming gone code: closed words conpty-sideload, conpty and sideload_fallback, SERVER_PID_REPORTED and the macOS carve-out, the schemas' OS words, help strings and doc comments; P3 lists them and P4 decides each against the masters' OS-target change.

Coverage gating per OS in section 10: per-OS gating justified by cfg(windows) and cfg(unix) compiling only on their own runner, and the COVERAGE_IGNORE regex's separator class that exists for Windows backslash paths; the regex is never widened.
The lint job's per-OS wording and the dev-host Windows- and macOS-target check-only clippy runs, which are no gates and lose their purpose.

Supply chain over the removed Windows dependencies: cargo deny with the trimmed deny.toml, deny-probes ending 14/14 banned with control clean, the sole-root tokio ban per sync crate, channel-tokio-free, and the release-check probes, each still ending its required line after the manifests change.

The e2e-home free-space floor in crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/mod.rs (cases at :481 and :501, the panic message built at :152): the cases must decide on a test-controlled free-space figure, never the runner's disk; the msrv job (ubuntu, Rust 1.96, unit suite) must be green; df -h /tmp is read before a stamped-home gate.

Linux behaviour unchanged, binding every test the removal touches: the typed exit set 0, 1, 2, 10-14, 20, 21; hook exit 0 with no body and no stderr; every Linux wire contract and closed word; the human-wins invariant and the NEVER-log floor.

No env, flag or feature seam may force a refusing peer-euid decision: the euid wiring of the three client seams stays held by no committed test, and the untestable zone of cross-OS-user peers stays as it is.
Live sessions are 0: everything runs on the fake agent, and CI never touches the real claude CLI.
The tag multi-os-final on the last three-OS commit, pushed to origin before any removal commit, and its resolving on origin as part of the acceptance.

The masters' OS-target change in the test-plan (the 3-OS CI matrix, the per-OS legs, the tier justification's 3 required OSes and multi-platform CI), and the re-pointing of the owner Windows-only live measurements, such as the vt100 panic's Windows byte reading: amendments the wrap writes, which this chunk's plan names as expected.
Pre-push and harness steps that run only for Windows or macOS leave with them; the local pre-push gate still checks the host's tools against ci.yml's pins.

body_fields.convention: each new or renamed test is named in snake_case as subject, condition, expected, and a critical-path scenario as path<N>_<slug>
table-driven cases in viola-e2e are a labelled case table in one #[test] with each assertion naming its label, adding no rstest manifest edge
a test decides on values it injects, never on the host's clock, disk or state: no sleep for synchronisation, no test-owned timer, waits keyed on logged events or offsets
each test makes its own --home through tempfile, sets env per child with Command::env and never std::env::set_var, and re-adds LLVM_PROFILE_FILE after env_clear
every workflow has permissions {} at the top and contents read per job, every uses SHA-pinned, no concurrency block, and rust-cache as the only cache, in ci.yml only
each tool has one version source, ci.yml's pins, and the pre-push gate checks the host's tools against them and installs nothing
each CI test job ends in viola-harness gate --require its suites, and every artifact leaves CI only behind the secret scan, with retention-days 7
no flaky test is tolerated: nextest retries 0, no retry budget, and no #[ignore] as a parking place
body_fields.home: section 10, Quality Gates & Coverage Targets (Zero-flakiness budget)

body_fields.convention: a harness command prints exactly one JSON document on stdout with exit 0, 1 or 2, never a human-only message
